facts.raw_span: A 35-year-old man was brought to the emergency department unconscious, with a Glasgow Coma Scale of 3
Glasgow Coma Scale of 3
found unconscious after smoking substances
polysubstance use for the past 10 years, including vapor inhalation via tin foil and pipe use
15 pack-year smoking history of tobacco
No family history available as patient was adopted
Urine drug screen: Positive for methamphetamines and opiates
Initial chest radiograph: Right lateral and basilar pneumothorax, approximately 30% in volume
CT angiography of chest (with and without contrast): Severe emphysema and bullous changes throughout the lungs, left lung lobe greater than right
Large bulla at posterior left lower lung measuring almost 18 cm
CT imaging of head and cervical spine without contrast: Negative
Alpha-1 antitrypsin level: Normal
HIV rapid antibody test: Nonreactive

support_spans: Severe emphysema and bullous changes throughout the lungs, left lung lobe greater than right
Large bulla at posterior left lower lung measuring almost 18 cm
concepts.why: The presence of large bullae in the lungs is a characteristic feature of bullous lung disease.

It explains the patient's initial unconscious state and the negative CT imaging of the head and cervical spine, suggesting a possible traumatic cause for the brain injury.
